title: ResourceType
description:
The catalog object: a kind of thing, not a thing. One GB200 NVL72 compute tray SKU is one ResourceType; the seventy-two of them in a rack are seventy-two Resources pointing at it.

This split is where partner data lands. Dell, Supermicro and ASUS supply almost entirely type data -- dimensions, power draw, port layout, coolant requirements -- and almost no instance data beyond serials. Without the split, every partner datasheet fact would be copied onto every unit, and correcting a published power figure would mean an UPDATE across thousands of rows instead of one.

resource_class.description: What kind of thing this is, coarsely. Deliberately a closed list: an open vocabulary here is how you end up with `switch`, `Switch`, `network-switch` and `tor` as four classes meaning one thing. Anything genuinely new is a contract change, which is a conversation worth having.

manufacturer.description: Who made it, as the name appears in contracts and on invoices: NVIDIA, Dell, Supermicro, ASUS, Vertiv, Amphenol. Not the reseller and not the integrator.

model.description: The manufacturer's model designation, verbatim. `GB200 NVL72` is a model; `gb200-nvl72-rack-v2-final` is a filename.

part_number.description: Orderable part number. This is the field procurement and the packing list agree on, which makes it the practical join between a delivery and an inventory record.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to manufacturer plus model when absent; present so a site can carry the name its operators already use.

identifiers.description: Type-level identity. Rare but real: a cable SKU with an EUI range, a GPU SKU with a PCI device ID. Instance identity belongs on Resource.

u_height.description: Rack units consumed. Fractional is allowed and necessary: a 1U-per-two-node sled is 0.5.

power.description: Nameplate figures from the datasheet, which are design limits rather than observed draw. Observed power is telemetry and does not belong in a catalog.

thermal_design_watts.description: TDP, which is the number cooling capacity is sized against.

cooling.description: How this type must be cooled. Present on the type because it is a property of the design, and it is what determines whether a rack can be placed in a given room at all.

method.description: dlc is direct-to-chip, which is the GB200/GB300 case.

coolant.description: pg25 and pg30 are propylene glycol mixes by volume, which is how the facility specifies them.

min_flow_lpm.description: Litres per minute required at design load. Below this the cold plate does not carry the heat, and this is the figure a commissioning check compares against.

port_templates.description: The ports every instance of this type has. A tray SKU with four OSFP cages produces four Port records per instance, and generating them from the type is what makes a cabling plan checkable before any hardware arrives.

name.description: Name pattern, with {n} substituted by index when count > 1: `OSFP{n}` yields OSFP1..OSFP4.

partner.description: The partner whose catalog this entry came from, when it is not the manufacturer -- an OEM rack integrator, for instance. Kept separate so partner-supplied data can be re-imported wholesale without touching NVIDIA-authored entries.

lifecycle.description: Where the SKU is in ITS life, which is a different question from where any instance is.

attributes.description: Type facts the model does not cover. Unlike labels, these are expected to be meaningful -- GPU count, memory capacity, NVLink generation -- and are the queue for the next contract version.
